title: Babel-Ashur
imageCaption: Babel-Ashur — full island reference preserved in the archive.
dek: An enormous island whose geography is defined by wild biomes and a central wound rather than by one dominant city.

facts.Expedition status: October mist rescue survived; temporary clearing, permanent recovery unconfirmed

body:
Babel-Ashur operates at a visibly different scale from the settlement-centered maps. Its full-island image is dominated by wild geography and a massive central scar or crater. The region’s identity therefore begins with destruction and biome, not a single civic center.

The survival crisis · May 2026

On 5 May 2026, Mya appeared battered amid a crisis severe enough to raise the possibility that nearly everyone else had already left. She insisted that all lands were worth saving and revealed that Babel’s Shard was not simply a tree, though the mechanism by which it protected the island remained unknown.

Arjahn was reported to be part of a losing vanguard. The record does not yet establish whether “Vanguard” was a formal organization, a temporary forward force, or simply a description of Arjahn’s position. In the same exchange, Mya said the gods believed there were too few Knights—or that those who remained were too weak—and presented a strategic choice: pass power and knowledge to a next wave, or reunite and prove the gods wrong.

The threat closes in · July 2026

By 29 July, Babel-Ashur’s monsters were moving closer and becoming hungrier and more aggressive. An unpetrified warrior, other adventurers, and roughly a dozen natives sheltered in a cave while a surviving seed or Shard remained central to the island’s future. The Knights were involved in a hunt connected to Death. None of this establishes what happened to the Vanguard after May; it shows only that the wider crisis continued to worsen.

Greyward Littoral

Babel-Ashur’s southern shore is named Greyward Littoral. Its dedicated map confirms that the island should be read at multiple scales: Babel-Ashur first, then the named coastal subregion and its expedition sites.

Luminar Spires

The Luminar Spires are a monumental coastal region saturated with unstable primal magic. During the reconnaissance recorded on 26 September 2026 (UTC), Elenia’s Daylight spell transformed into a reversed-gravity effect, the formations glowed after the spell ended, and the Spires twinkled like stars at sunset.

The western mist

The same expedition investigated a vast sickly-green mist covering essentially the island’s western portion. Elenia says it entered through a rift and distinguishes it from the Pale Man’s Haze. Gartina observed unidentified figures moving beneath it; Arjahn’s radiant test burned it away only temporarily before it regenerated. Proximity does not establish that the mist and Spires share an origin.

A region read at multiple scales

Babel-Ashur’s full map should be read from region to subregion to expedition site. The island-scale crater establishes a wound vast enough to organize the landscape. The Greyward Littoral gives the southern coast its own identity. The Luminar Spires then become one specific field of unstable magic rather than a synonym for all of Babel-Ashur. This hierarchy keeps a single dramatic encounter from flattening an enormous island.

The same caution applies to the west. The green mist covered essentially the western portion of the island during the recorded reconnaissance, but its vertical limit, underground reach, inhabitants, and permanence were not established. Gartina’s flight above it, Arjahn’s perception, and the radiant test are local observations—not a complete map of the phenomenon.

Survival changes the meaning of distance

By May and July 2026, distance on Babel-Ashur was measured in defensible shelter, proximity of monsters, remaining allies, and access to the surviving seed or Shard. A cave holding natives and adventurers could matter as much as a formal city because survival pressure had compressed public life into places that could still be defended.

The Luminar expedition adds a different kind of foothold: shared method. Scribonia recognized limits, Gartina tested the environment and performed rescue, Arjahn risked direct observation, Elenia supplied prior knowledge, Olokun carried strategic history, and Nymera provided practical assistance. Their achievement was not conquest. It was the creation of a first disciplined record future expeditions can challenge and extend.

An island not reducible to one disaster

Babel-Ashur remains under severe pressure, but the surviving record shows people making choices rather than merely awaiting destruction. Defenders hold a losing line, residents shelter together, explorers test routes, and knowledge passes between generations of adventurers. The central scar, western mist, Spires, Littoral, monsters, and Shard may interact, but the archive does not force them into one cause without evidence.

The current government, surviving settlements, safe routes between subregions, exact scale of evacuation, fate of the Vanguard, and relationship among the island’s crises remain open. Protected divine explanations are intentionally absent from the public entry.

The people who kept the seeds

The recovered expedition account follows a rescue from the caverns into a community at Skylight Refuge. A nomad entrusts Elenia with a golden seed after Mya’s light frees the captives. At a later meal, Kvethe, Quille, Omari and Kyrin speak for themselves about scattered tribes, interrupted succession, lost farms and the daily labor of survival. Rhea is also named among the listeners. Their stories are testimony, not a complete reconstruction of the island’s ancient history.

Kyrin names the floating island Ashur and remembers the waters of its tree. Omari repeats stories learned from elders while explicitly admitting not having seen that island. The accounts include both memory and inherited tradition, without treating them as interchangeable proof.

August · the Refuge holds, with losses

The hunters’ approach forces a divided defense. Olokun, Elenia and Scribonia draw threats away; Arjahn, Eugene and Nymera remain between the other attackers and the civilians. Eugene finds a fighting position away from the refugees, but the defenders are soon spending their reserves to survive.

Eugene’s Wish destroys two attackers and Arjahn revives Nymera after her first death. The diversion returns badly wounded, followed by two beasts. In the renewed fighting Nymera is reduced to ash; Eugene and Scribonia kill the remaining creatures. The narrator confirms that Skylight Refuge is safe, while warning that not everyone is. The ashes are collected for a later attempt to restore her.

This is the immediate history behind the later turn toward the mountain. Defending a shelter has bought survival without removing the enemy stronghold or ending the work of recovery. Follow the defense through its different witnesses →

The mountain assault

In the account posted on 29 August 2026 (UTC), Scribonia and Eugene sustain two weather systems while Elenia and Arjahn redirect water and cast earthquakes. Rain, melting snow, fissures and avalanches reshape the cavern-bearing mountain; lava leaks near the caves and smoke obscures the result. Arjahn carries Eugene away from the flooding ground. The mountain is visibly altered, but the scene does not establish that Abyss was killed or that all captives and civilians escaped.

At the gathering posted on 26 September (UTC), companions describe having collapsed and flooded the stronghold, then turn toward the western mist and Luminar Spires. These are dates of the surviving account; exact in-world dates remain unresolved.

October · the mist turns rescue against itself

The October expedition begins at a safer Skylight Refuge: ordinary wildlife is returning to its surroundings. That local improvement does not make the jungle safe. Wren, Scribonia, Olokun, Arjahn, Nymera and Ryvyt encounter a giant blind salamander near the route toward the Spires and mist. Its breath paralyzes companions and Olokun is badly wounded. Ryvyt’s healing and restoration help keep him alive; Olokun lands the final blow. A second rush through the undergrowth proves to be a passing boar.

At the coast, the green mist has nearly reached the shore. The attempt to investigate becomes a rescue as visions of loved ones draw people away from their tethers and turn companions into apparent monsters. Ryvyt dispels Nymera’s effect before Scribonia’s Wish clears the mist for miles. Abyss appears and withdraws during the clearing, answering the earlier uncertainty about his permanent destruction: the mountain assault did not end his activity.

The company survives, but its members need care, rest and difficult conversations. Scribonia collapses and Nymera carries him toward the refuge under Arjahn’s escort. The recorded gain is knowledge of the mist and some ways to resist it. Its permanent removal, the rift’s condition and the island’s broader recovery remain unestablished.

October · an offer refused after the clearing

A figure beside the crystal pillars is first mistaken for Abyss, then identifies himself as Dumuzi. He invites the exhausted adventurers to join him and uses Oya’s safety as an inducement. Olokun and Ryvyt refuse; Scribonia rejects the bargain while challenging his account of what a better world would require. Arjahn answers that a wounded world should be healed and that no single will should choose for everyone. Nymera quietly insists that an imperfect world still needs protection.

Dumuzi also claims that Aria is not dead and is better than before. That is later testimony, not a witnessed return or a reason to erase Talan’s recorded killing. A vision is received during the encounter, but its contents are not available as reviewed text in this packet. The witnessed responses and continuing refusals do not authorize an invented account of what it showed.

The scene is posted on 18 October 2026 in New York, ending at 03:54 UTC on 19 October. These dates place the surviving account; they do not establish a local calendar date within Fenumion.

Mark of the Wild · the cost of gathering

Reconnaissance and supply gathering continue around the larger expeditions. The Mark of the Wild hunts connect Aravil’s field skills, Aerrow’s scouting, Arjahn’s protection and the company’s crafting and building needs. Victories bring components; failed harvests, retreats and deaths show how fragile that work remains.

The February two-person hunt ends with Aerrow dead after an earlier Revivify. The main quest later records Elenia raising him. June and July gathering serves a shelter now shared with rescued people; early October ends with healing and a visit to the coast. These are distinct outings, not one uninterrupted expedition or a general claim that all wildlife belongs to Death.
